newsitem.title: USA: DC eyes too much money from school closings--paper.
newsitem.headline: DC eyes too much money from school closings--paper.

text.p: A proposal to close 16 District of Columbia shools may not achieve the desired financial results, the Washington Post reported Monday.
The school system's emergency board of trustees estimates the value of all 16 schools at $42 million, the Post reported.

But real estate specialists, community activists and others familiar with the schools say the estimate is highly optimistic, the Post reported. A number of factors, including market conditions, zoning, historic status and environmental concerns, decrease the trustees board's estimate, the Post reported.
Suzanne Conrad, a board of trustees staff member who is coordinating the real estate program, defended the value estimates. "I think those numbers are not unreasonable at all," she told the Post.
